newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL CS JULY 16 SUGAR STOCKS CONTINUE BELOW 1996.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL CS JULY 16 SUGAR STOCKS CONTINUE BELOW 1996.

text.p: Brazilian sugar stocks in the center-south growing region were around 1.09 million tonnes on July 16, around 496,000 tonnes less than at the same stage last year, independent consultant DataNet Agri-Commodities said.
Since the start of the center-south harvest, around 1.68 million tonnes have been delivered to the domestic market and 1.14 million tonnes to the international market, DataNet said.
This represents an increase of 88,000 tonnes to the home market in comparison with last year and a rise of 358,000 tonnes sent overseas.
Sugar exports have played a key role in slowing down the fall in prices on the domestic market compared to last year, DataNet said.
In the last week in July, prices for crystal sugar ex-factory including tax reached 12.57 reais per 50-bag against 14.86 reais at the same stage last year, a drop of 15 percent.
Prices have already this year been up to 24 percent down on last season, DataNet said.
Actual sugar production to July 16 reached 3.36 million tonnes, down 2.30 percent on the 3.44 million tonnes produced to the same stage in 1996/97.
Production has picked up from previous fortnightly periods with the 900,000 tonnes between July 2-16 comparing with 720,000 tonnes in the two weeks to July 1 and 510,000 tonnes between June 2-15.
In the fortnight period to July 16, around 433,000 tonnes were destined for the domestic market and 321,000 tonnes to the international market.
Total alcohol production continues to run well ahead of last year, reaching 4.62 million cubic meters, up 8.13 percent from 4.27 million in 1996/97.
However, the rise is almost entirely due to increased output of hydrous alcohol given production of anhydrous alcohol of 1.35 million cubic meters is on a par with last year.

The heightened production is due to the price table drawn up by the National Combustible Fuels Department for hydrous alcohol which guarantees prices are not hit by seasonal supply variations, DataNet said.
